findings.claim: every episode that opened before 17:00 CT the prior evening is re-recorded, with ordinal 1, on every read … all 14 RTH-L episodes opened before the level existed … Watch: rows with `opened_at_ms < formed_at_ms` = 0
findings.evidence: (a) kernel/detector_recorder.go:99-107 `NewEpisodesSince` keeps only `e.OpenedAtMs > lastOpenedMs && e.ClosedAtMs != 0`; `last` = MAX(opened_at_ms) over rows with opened_at_ms ≥ session-day start (touch_outcomes.go:259-262). So pre-day episodes are re-recorded on every read ONLY while the (trader,symbol,price) has no in-day episode yet; the first in-day episode raises `last` ≥ dayMs and silences them. The RTH-L copies (3,7,9,11,11…) and VWAP's 199 rows = 199 episodes (price changes per read, so the price-keyed watermark never matches) are both consistent with this. (b) sqlite ro on bars: the 09-03 RTH low 29199.25 printed on the 08:36:00 CT bar; the 14th RTH-L episode opened at 08:36:00 CT (`GROUP BY opened_at_ms` → last row 2026-09-03 08:36:00, 11 copies). Under the Rec-1 rule `scan from max(FormedAtMs, watermark)` that episode is ON the formation bar, not before it: 13 of 14 are pre-formation.
findings.correction: "…re-recorded, with ordinal 1, on every read until that level records its first episode opening after the session-day start (NewEpisodesSince, detector_recorder.go:102); dynamic lines never reach that point because their price moves." And: "13 of 14 RTH-L episodes opened before the 08:36 CT bar that printed 29199.25; the 14th opened on that bar — all 14 before it was a PRIOR-day low."

overall: The section's verdict survives this pass. Its three load-bearing code claims are exactly what the code says: the recorder scans the whole 2,000-bar scope (trader/detector_record.go:57; svp.go:47) against a session-day-scoped watermark and ordinal (store/touch_outcomes.go:254-266, :73-84) and never reads DetectedLevel.FormedAtMs (levels.go:89); PDH/PDL/PDC are a CT calendar-day bucket behind a 900-bar guard with `k < todayCal` (levels_multiday.go:15, :146-160, :222, :229-237) — I re-derived the 08-26 +218.5/+37.5 calendar-vs-session gap and the 09-02 truncated-bucket PDH 29317.25 (1,082 bars ≥ 900, true high 29571 at 00:xx CT) from the bars table; BuildCandidatePool writes score 0/grade ''/`{}` for every cut row (detector_recorder.go:70-73; 181/181 and 360/360 in the store); and grep finds zero grade consumers in the five downstream files. The store corroborates P1–P6 and P11 (12/1.0/strict on a5b7662e; 677 rows = 423 episodes, RTH-L 140→14 with up to 11 copies opened 22:10 09-02–08:36 09-03; arms 23–37 and 6-of-67 marketable; one RTH-L arm). Nothing the report recommends has already shipped: no fix touched the recorder files after 09-03 (git log), the two-day audit's C6 only saw zero rows, and the post-soak plan has no session-day-PDH item. What did not survive: the Evidence-Basis diff command does not produce the output claimed and auto_trader_planner.go's cited lines are +14 versus the running binary (WRONG); the Surprise-1 cancel breakdown is 4/7/8/1 not 5/8/7 (WRONG); '11 of 12 reads' is 14 of 15 detector reads (WRONG); the HTF ×1.2 scope omits HTF-tagged EQH/EQL (WRONG); and a run of citation slips (auto_trader_dayplan.go:20, INDEX.md:34→:44, 'can never pass' at :218-220, verify 'F6', POC as Tier-1, ~9 h→8 h). The more consequential omissions are rulings the recommendations restate or reverse without naming them: Rec 2 is class 64's own unmet law (AUDIT-CHECKLIST.md:1402-1405); Rec 9/3 should route through the class-45 resolver rather than a 12,000-bar 1m fetch (the store already holds 1d back to 2019); Rec 11 is demotion-queue item 8 and target_only is prompt text + a WARN, refusing nothing; Rec 5 reverses the 2026-08-27 ±2σ emission ruling (00e3b370) and the A2 eVWAP re-anchor; Rec 6 re-rules a knob the owner already set off-default with a prior C6 sweep on record. The [A] labels are honest except line 11's command claim and the level_state 'PDH' identification, which is a tape-corroborated inference rather than a read. Net: fix the four WRONG lines and add the ruling citations; the section's problems, refutations of the prior review, and 'fix the instrument first' ordering all stand.
